issue_context.title: [BUG] Locator.waitFor is leaking DOM nodes
issue_context.body:
### System info - Playwright Version: v1.31 - Operating System: Windows 11 - Browser: Edge/WebView2 - Other info: It is probably for all system and browsers, but checked only in this one ### Source code - [ ] I provided exact source code that allows reproducing the issue locally. **Test file (pseudocode)** ```js it('should check element is not leaking', async ({ page }) => { await Promise.all([ () => page.locator('//*[@id="should_not_leak'div"]').waitFor({ state: 'attached' }), () => page.setContent(`
`) ]) }); ``` **Steps** - [Run the test] - [...] **Expected** There is no detached div element at the end of the test **Actual** Playwright leaks element(s) found by locators, if there is `waitFor` called on them, due to internally used Handles and not disposing them.
comments: @dolezel since this is a regression, let me land a proper fix instead. Appreciate the PR though!

review_comments: I believe omitReturnValue was supposed to avoid handle allocation but got lost during refactorings. Let's either remove 'omitReturnValue' and all dispose here as you do or make 'omitReturnValue' work.
